d.x: Men can ejaculate between 0.1 and 10 milliliters of semen on average.

d.g: To sexually stimulate (someone) so that they eject fluid from the urethra.

d.g: The uttering of a short, sudden exclamation or prayer, or the exclamation or prayer uttered.
The act of ejecting or suddenly throwing fluid or some other substance from a duct or other body structure.
A reflex in human beings and other mammals in response to sexual stimulation involving the forcible ejection from the urethra of, in males, semen; and, in females, vaginal fluid.

ejaculation.e: From French éjaculation, borrowed from Latin ēiaculārī.

d.g: A person or thing that ejaculates.

ejaculator.e: English ejaculate English -or English ejaculator From ejaculate + -or.

ejection.e: From Middle French éjection, from Latin eiectio.

d.g: One who, or that which, ejects or dispossesses.
A jet jump for lifting water or withdrawing air from a space.
ejector seat: a pilot's seat in an airplane that can be forcibly ejected in the case of an emergency; then the pilot descends by parachute.
That part of the mechanism of a breech-loading firearm which ejects the empty shell.

ejector.e: English eject English -or English ejector From eject + -or.

d.g: To compel (a person or persons) to leave.

d.g: To throw out or remove forcefully.

eject.e: From Middle French éjecter, from Latin ēiectus, perfect passive participle of ēiciō (“to throw out”), or from ēiectō, the frequentative form of the same verb, from ē-, combining form of ex (“out”), + iaciō (“to throw”).
